inline.s: [Now I, for the sake of all sentient beings, proclaim this sutra and its Dharma, causing them to behold Amitabha Buddha and all that belongs to his land. Whatever should be done, all of it may be sought therein. Do not, after my entry into nirvana, give rise to doubt again.]

Now, for the sake of all sentient beings, I proclaim this sutra and its Dharma, causing them to behold Amitabha Buddha and all that belongs to his land. Whatever should be done (that is, the faith, the vows, and the practice by which one seeks birth in the Western Land of Utmost Bliss) must be striven after with all one's might. You must not, after my entry into nirvana, give rise to doubt again.

[In ages to come, the scriptures and the Way will be utterly extinguished. Out of compassion and pity, I will specially preserve this sutra, to remain for a hundred years. Whatever sentient beings encounter this sutra will, according to their own wishes, all attain deliverance.]

In ages to come, the scriptures and the Way will be utterly extinguished. Out of compassion and pity, I will specially preserve this sutra, to abide for a hundred years more. Whatever sentient beings encounter this sutra will, according to their own wishes, all attain deliverance.
[The extinction of the scriptures and the Way] The Jingying Commentary says:

“In ages to come, when the scriptures and the Way are extinguished — this sets forth the matter of the Dharma's extinction in the future. Śākyamuni's True Dharma lasts five hundred years, the Semblance Dharma a thousand years, and the Final Dharma ten thousand years. When all of these have passed, it is called complete extinction.”
Master Shandao's Verses of Praise for Rebirth says:
“When the Three Jewels are extinguished after ten thousand years, this sutra remains for a hundred years.”

[True Dharma, Semblance Dharma, Final Dharma] The Buddha-Dharma is divided into three periods: the period of the True Dharma, the period of the Semblance Dharma, and the period of the Final Dharma. In the period of the True Dharma, although the Buddha has entered nirvana, the Dharma and its forms are unchanged: there is teaching, there is practice, and there are those who realize the fruit — this is called the period of the True Dharma. In the period of the Semblance Dharma, semblance means likeness: it resembles the True Dharma but is not the True Dharma. In this period there is teaching and there is practice, but those who realize the fruit are already very few. In the period of the Final Dharma, final means feeble: this period declines into feebleness, and there is only teaching without practice, and no one at all who realizes the fruit.

[For a Tathagata to appear in the world is hard to meet and hard to see. The scriptures and the Way of the Buddhas are hard to obtain and hard to hear. To meet a good spiritual friend and, having heard the Dharma, be able to practice it — this too is difficult. If one hears this sutra and believes, delights in, and upholds it, of all difficulties there is none that surpasses this.]

For a Tathagata to appear in the world is hard to meet and hard to see. The scriptures and the Way of the Buddhas are hard to obtain and hard to hear. To meet a good spiritual friend and, having heard the Dharma, be able to practice it — this too is difficult. If one hears this sutra and believes, delights in, and upholds it, of all difficulties there is none that surpasses this.

[If there are sentient beings who, hearing the Buddha's name, have a pure and compassionate mind, leap up with joy, feel the hairs of their bodies stand on end, or shed tears, it is all because in past lives they cultivated the Buddha-way; therefore they are not ordinary people.]

If there are sentient beings who, hearing the name of Amitabha Buddha, have a pure and compassionate mind, leap up with joy, feel the hairs of their bodies stand on end, or shed tears, it is all because in past lives they cultivated the Buddha-way; therefore they are not ordinary people.
[Hearing the Buddha's name] That is, hearing the name of Amitabha Buddha.
The Sutra of Immeasurable Life as Spoken by the Buddha (the Wei translation) has
“having heard the name of that Buddha”
and the Assembly of the Tathagata of Immeasurable Life (the Tang translation) has
“hearing the name of that Buddha”
and the Sutra of the Adornment of Immeasurable Life, the Great Vehicle, as Spoken by the Buddha (the Song translation) has
“having heard the name of the Buddha of Immeasurable Life”

[If, hearing the Buddha's name, one is dubious in mind and, with regard to the Buddha's scriptural words, believes nothing at all, such persons have all come from the evil paths; their past calamity is not yet exhausted, and they are not yet to be delivered. Hence their minds are dubious and they do not believe and turn toward it.]

If, hearing the name of Amitabha Buddha, one is dubious in mind and, with regard to the Buddha's scriptural words, believes nothing at all, such persons have all come from the evil paths; their past calamity is not yet exhausted, and they are not yet to be delivered. Hence their minds are dubious and they cannot believe and accept it.

[The Buddha told Maitreya: The unsurpassed Dharma of the Buddhas and Tathagatas — the deeply profound Dharma of the ten powers, the fearlessnesses, the unobstructed, and the unattached, and the bodhisattva Dharmas such as the pāramitās — is not easily encountered. Those able to expound the Dharma also find it hard to reveal. Those of firm and deep faith are, again, rarely to be met.]

The Buddha told Bodhisattva Maitreya: The unsurpassed Dharma of the Buddhas and Tathagatas — the deeply profound Dharma of the ten powers, the fearlessnesses, the unobstructed, and the unattached, and the bodhisattva Dharmas such as the pāramitās — is by no means easy to encounter. Those able to expound the Dharma also find it hard to reveal. Those of firm and deep faith, likewise, are not easy to find.

[Now I proclaim in accordance with principle this vast and subtle Dharma-gate, which is praised by all Buddhas. I entrust it to you, that you may make great protection for it, for the benefit of all sentient beings throughout the long night. Do not let sentient beings sink and fall into the five destinies, to suffer every kind of peril and pain.]

Now I proclaim in accordance with principle this vast and subtle Pure Land Dharma-gate, which is praised by all Buddhas. I entrust it to you, that you may make great protection for it, so as to benefit all sentient beings throughout the long night. Do not let them sink and fall into the five destinies, to suffer every kind of peril and pain.
[I entrust it to you]

Bodhisattva Maitreya is a bodhisattva with but one life remaining, who presently dwells in the Inner Court of the Tuṣita Heaven. After four thousand years (that is, five billion six hundred seventy million years in human reckoning), he will descend and be born in the human world, and beneath the dragon-flower tree in the Hua-lin Grove he will realize Buddhahood; following after Śākyamuni Buddha, he is the fifth Tathagata of the Worthy Kalpa.
“The Buddha told Maitreya:

Now I proclaim in accordance with principle this vast and subtle Dharma-gate, which is praised by all Buddhas. I entrust it to you, that you may make great protection for it, for the benefit of all sentient beings throughout the long night.”
This shows that after Bodhisattva Maitreya realizes Buddhahood in this Sahā world, he too will proclaim and spread the Sutra of Immeasurable Life.
[The long night] A simile for the long darkness of ignorance through which ordinary beings, from beginningless kalpas, transmigrate in birth and death.

[You should diligently cultivate practice and comply with my teaching. You should be filial to the Buddha and constantly remember the kindness of the teacher. You should cause this Dharma to abide long and not be extinguished. You should steadfastly uphold it, and not destroy or lose it. You must not, out of delusion, add to or subtract from the sutra-Dharma.]

You should diligently cultivate practice and comply with my teaching. You should be filial to the Buddha and constantly remember the kindness of the original teacher. You should cause this Dharma to abide long and not be extinguished. You should steadfastly uphold it, and not destroy or lose it. You must not recklessly add to or subtract from the sutra-Dharma.

[If you are mindful without cease, you will attain the Way swiftly. My Dharma is thus; thus do I speak. The practice of the Tathagata you too should follow. Cultivate merit and goodness, and seek birth in the Pure Land.]

For one who is mindful of the name of Amitabha Buddha without cease, thought following thought, the Way is swiftly attained. My Dharma is thus; thus do I speak. The practice of the Tathagata you too should follow. Cultivate merit and goodness, and seek birth in the Western Land of Utmost Bliss.
[Mindful without cease] “Constantly mindful” means constantly mindful of the name of Amitabha Buddha; “without cease” means thought following thought without interruption.

blocks.text: 47. The Fortunate and Wise First Hear It

inline.s: [At that time the World-Honored One spoke in verse, saying:
Then the World-Honored One spoke these verses:
Had you not in former lives cultivated merit and wisdom,
you could not hear
(you would not hear the Pure Land Dharma-gate, or, having heard it, you would be unable to give rise to faith and take it in)
this true Dharma; but having once made offerings to the Tathagatas, you can joyfully believe in this matter.
The evil, the proud, the indolent, and those of wrong views find it hard to believe the Tathagata's subtle Dharma; like the blind who forever dwell in darkness, they cannot guide others on the road.
Only if in former lives one served the Buddhas and planted every root of goodness can one cultivate this world-saving deed
(the Pure Land Dharma-gate);
having heard it, one upholds and copies it, recites it, praises and expounds it, and makes offerings.
[The world-saving deed] The Pure Land Dharma-gate can broadly deliver sentient beings from birth and death, and so it is called “the world-saving deed.”

If thus with one mind you seek the pure land, you will surely be born in the Land of Utmost Bliss; though a great fire filled the three thousand worlds, riding the Buddha's majestic power you would transcend it all.

The Tathagata's deep and vast ocean of wisdom only Buddhas with Buddhas can know; śrāvakas for koṭis of kalpas pondering the Buddha's wisdom, though they exhaust their spiritual powers, cannot fathom it.
The Tathagata's merits the Buddha knows of himself; only the World-Honored One can reveal them. A human body is hard to gain, a Buddha is hard to meet
(hard to encounter),
and to hear the Dharma with faith and wisdom is the hardest of the hard.

If all sentient beings are to become Buddhas, their practice must surpass Samantabhadra's, and they must ascend to the other shore; therefore you learned and wise ones of broad knowledge should believe my teaching, and receive it as the truth I speak.

Having been so fortunate as to hear this wondrous Dharma, you should constantly recollect the Buddha and give rise to joy; upholding it, broadly cross the stream of birth and death — the Buddha says that such a one is a true good friend.]

[Upholding it and broadly crossing the stream of birth and death] To receive and uphold this sutra and, by this Pure Land Dharma-gate, to broaden and deliver those sentient beings who are drowning in birth and death. “Zhi liu” — “those of such a kind” — means a certain person or thing of one and the same class. “The stream of birth and death” is the current of birth and death, that is, the sentient beings who are drowning in birth and death. [The Buddha says that such a one is a true good friend] The Buddha says that such a person is truly a good friend of sentient beings (a good spiritual friend).

blocks.text: 48. The Benefits of Hearing the Sutra

inline.s: [At that time, when the World-Honored One had spoken this sutra and its Dharma, in the heavens and the human world there were twelve thousand nayuta koṭis of sentient beings who, far from dust and defilement, attained the pure Dharma-eye. Twenty koṭis of sentient beings attained the fruit of Anāgāmin. Six thousand eight hundred bhikṣus, their outflows all exhausted, attained liberation of mind. Forty koṭis of bodhisattvas abided in non-retrogression from the unsurpassed bodhi, adorning themselves with the merit of their great vows. Twenty-five koṭis of sentient beings attained the patience of non-retrogression. Four koṭi-koṭis of hundreds of thousands of sentient beings, who had never before given rise to the intention of unsurpassed bodhi, now for the first time gave rise to it. Planting all roots of goodness and vowing to be born in the Land of Utmost Bliss and to see Amitabha Buddha, they will all be reborn in that Tathagata's land. Each in a different region, they will in turn become Buddhas, all of the same name, the Tathagata Wonderful Sound.]

At that time, when the World-Honored One had finished speaking this sutra and its Dharma, in the heavens and the human world there were twelve thousand times ten thousand million sentient beings who, far from dust and defilement
(affliction)

, attained the pure Dharma-eye. Twenty koṭis of sentient beings attained the fruit of Anāgāmin. Six thousand eight hundred bhikṣus, their afflictions all exhausted, attained liberation of mind. Forty koṭis of bodhisattvas abided in non-retrogression from the unsurpassed bodhi, adorning themselves with the merit of their great vows. Twenty-five koṭis of sentient beings attained the patience of non-retrogression. Four koṭi-koṭis of hundreds of thousands of sentient beings, who had never before given rise to the intention of unsurpassed bodhi, now for the first time gave rise to it. They planted all roots of goodness and, vowing to be born in the Land of Utmost Bliss and to see Amitabha Buddha, will all be reborn in the Western Land of Utmost Bliss. Each in a different region of the ten directions, they will in turn become Buddhas, all of the same name, the Tathagata Wonderful Sound.
[Their afflictions all exhausted] They attained the fruit of Arhatship.

[Furthermore, in the Buddha-lands of the ten directions, whether those now being born or those to be born in the future who see Amitabha Buddha — in each case there are eighty thousand koṭi nayuta persons who attain the prophecy and the Dharma-patience, and accomplish the unsurpassed bodhi. Those sentient beings, all through the karmic conditions of Amitabha Buddha's past vows, alike attain rebirth in the Western Land of Utmost Bliss.]

Furthermore, in the Buddha-lands of the ten directions, whether those now being born or those to be born in the future who see Amitabha Buddha — in each case there are eighty thousand times ten thousand million persons who attain the prophecy and win the patience of the non-arising of dharmas, and accomplish the unsurpassed bodhi (perfectly realizing the Buddha-fruit). These sentient beings, all through the karmic conditions of Amitabha Buddha's past vows, alike attain rebirth in the Western Land of Utmost Bliss.
[Koṭi] A unit of number used in ancient India, equivalent to what is now called a hundred million.

[At that time the three-thousand-great-thousand world trembled in six ways and manifested all manner of rare and miraculous transformations, emitting a great light that universally illumined the ten directions. Furthermore, the gods in the heavens played wondrous music and uttered sounds of rejoicing. Even all the gods of the form realm heard it, and exclaimed that such a thing had never been. Measureless wondrous flowers came raining down in profusion.]

At that time the three-thousand-great-thousand world trembled in six ways and manifested all manner of rare and miraculous transformations, emitting a great light that universally illumined the ten directions. Furthermore, the gods in the heavens played wondrous music and uttered sounds of rejoicing. Even all the gods of the form realm heard it, and exclaimed that such a thing had never been. Measureless wondrous flowers came raining down in profusion.

[The Venerable Ānanda, Bodhisattva Maitreya, and all the bodhisattvas and śrāvakas, the gods, nāgas, and the eight classes of beings, the whole great assembly, hearing what the Buddha had spoken, all rejoiced greatly, believed and accepted it, and practiced it in accordance.]

The Venerable Ānanda, Bodhisattva Maitreya, and all the bodhisattvas and śrāvakas, the gods, nāgas, and the eight classes of beings, the whole great assembly, hearing what the Buddha had spoken, all rejoiced greatly, believed and accepted it, and practiced it in accordance.
